full_judgment:
III. Because Kabala deeds had been executed and registered in 1981 creates a strong presumption that the registration authority was satisfied that the executant was a valid citizen and national of Bangladesh. The learned Single Judge failed to take into account the legal aspect of the matter and the title was established in Title Suit No. 7 of 1990 decreeing the same in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner and thus fell into a substantial errors and omission on the face of, the record causing a miscarriage of jus-tice which deserves for review consideration by this Court." 

 9. Mr. Nikhil Kumar Saha, the learned senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant taking us through the judgment and decree dated 09.11.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3747 of 2002, judgments and decrees of the appellate Court as well as trial Court, the other materials on record, contends that the High Court Division has committed illegality in totally misconceiving the case of the appellant upon mis-reading and misconstruing the evidence and materials on record and thereby mis-directed beyond the law and facts of the case in passing the erroneous judgment occasioning serious miscarriage of justice and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. The learned senior Counsel contends further that the High Court Division erred in law in not taking into account of the fact that Kabala deeds had been executed and registered in 1981 creates a strong presumption that the registration authority was satisfied that the executant was a valid citizen and national of Bangladesh, but the High Court Division did neither advert nor reverse the concurrent findings of the trial Court as well as appellate Court below in this regard and as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside.
